# AI agents: the spec

## Contents

- Capabilities
- Using an agent in a workflow
- Spec fields
- Writing instructions

## Capabilities

The editor never offers a single tool. It offers capabilities, each a fixed set of tools. The set
was harvested by adding each capability alone to a throwaway lab agent and reading the stored draft:

| Capability | Tools | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| Manage Requests | 17 (`system_adesk_*`, user search) | **acts**: creates and edits requests; creates notes (cannot edit or delete them), messages, approvals |
| Send Envelopes | 6 (`system_esign_*`) | **acts**: sends, updates and voids envelopes |
| Find Agreements | 8 (search, read, hierarchy, field definitions) | reads |
| Generate Documents | 5 (`system_docgen_*`, `system_dtl_*`) | **acts**: creates documents |
| Party Insights | 3 (party snapshot, reporting) | reads |
| Ask the User | 5 (`system_hitl_*`, user info) | **pauses** for a person |
| Review Documents | 3 (AI-Assisted Review chat, canvases, Word inspection) | reads |
| Search Salesforce / HubSpot / Dynamics 365 | 4 each (the same `system_connected_data_*` tools) | reads; needs a connected org |

Adding an acting capability shows a banner: "This agent has been granted write permissions and may
take actions that create, modify, or delete data". A spec that uses one must say `"acts": true`.
An agent with no capability is allowed: it works from the prompt alone (the Address Splitter).

## Using an agent in a workflow

The **Execute AI Agent** step (`moduleName: UseCustomAIAgent`, `type: DS-UseCustomAIAgent`):

- `config: { resourceKey, agentName }` — the agent by key. `userImpersonationParticipantId` and
  `userImpersonationType: "workflowPreparer"` appear only on an API-started export; request and
  event starts carry neither.
- `input.content` — the prompt, as the editor's rich-text document; a variable is a `mention` node
  (`{ id: "TicketFriendlyId_<trigger>", label: "Request ID" }`).
- `output` — one entry per `maestroOutputs` item, keyed `<name>_<stepId>`, type **String** for a
  string, **Boolean** for a boolean (both seen in a real export) and **Float** for a number
  (harvested in the builder, 2026-10-24: docs/WORKFLOW-BUILDER-WORKFLOWS.md, "Three shapes harvested"). A
  Float output takes the numeric branch operators (`{ "if": { "field": "renewal.days_to_deadline",
  "lte": 30 } }`); only a String output fills a document field or a text tab. The outputs are also
  the workflow's variables.
- The config instance saves `{ resourceKey, agentName, content }`.

Later steps read an output exactly like a form answer: a branch's left operand
(`risk_level_<stepId>`, as a real export's "risk_level = RED"), a Multi Branch's `switchKey`
(`route_to_<stepId>`), a request message's mention, a document field.

In a spec:

```json
{ "agent": "third-party-paper-triage", "as": "triage", "prompt": "Triage request {{TicketId}} ({{TicketTitle}})." },
{ "switch": { "field": "triage.route_to", "cases": [ { "is": "General Counsel", "steps": [ { "status": "General Counsel Review" } ] } ] } },
{ "message": { "to": ["submitter"], "body": "{{triage.risk_summary}}" } }
```

**The agent does not travel in the package.** Import keeps the step's `resourceKey` as written, so
the agent must already exist, published, in the importing account. `npm run workflow:check` warns
for each agent a workflow needs. `captures/agent-create.ts` creates one (`--key=<key>` updates an existing one
in place, as a new revision); then compile the workflow with `agentKeys`, or re-pick the agent in the imported step.

**Publishing a workflow with an agent step needs the AI disclaimer**, every time: the pre-run check returns
Docusign's own words ("This workflow runs without a person in the loop…") and a version, and the person who publishes
must agree to them explicitly. Show those words as returned, never tick the box for anyone (the workflow spec reference, *Publishing*).

**The prompt is the agent's only input from the workflow**, and it holds at most 200 characters (a variable counts
about 20): six to eight values. Write the instructions about those values only: an agent told to check a salary the
prompt does not carry reports it "missing" (acceptance 8). Values a signer types into an envelope are not offered to
the compiler's prompt; collect them on a web form first.

Four refusals:
- a chat-only agent (`"inWorkflow": false`): the step does not offer it;
- an agent that can **Ask the User**: inside a workflow nobody answers, so the run would wait;
- `{{TicketFriendlyId}}` (the Request ID) on a request-TYPE start: only a status start declares it,
  so use `{{TicketId}}` there;
- a Boolean output into a document field: only a text output fills one.

Two cautions from the help (2026-10-28), not yet measured in a run:
- **Acting tools may wait for a person, as Ask the User does.** The capabilities' own descriptions
  read "Create approvals with human sign-off … Edit intake forms with human sign-off" (Manage Requests)
  and "Send envelopes with human approval" (Send Envelopes), and "In fully automated workflows, agents
  have limited capabilities and stricter safety controls" ([capabilities](https://support.docusign.com/s/document-item?language=en_US&bundleId=map781cab17-20ee-4e52-a109-43201480b341&topicId=ref142a0947-2ecb-48dd-835b-cf10ac4714fa.html&_LANG=enus),
  [automated](https://support.docusign.com/s/document-item?language=en_US&bundleId=map781cab17-20ee-4e52-a109-43201480b341&topicId=con507f961a-731d-4763-9d03-2432603d1ae4.html&_LANG=enus)). The workflow agents here that hold one
  (third-party-paper-triage) carries a read-only rule in their instructions, and the
  triage reads only. A run that waits on such a step would point here.
- **An agent cannot read Agreement Manager's clause extractions.** "Extracted clauses are not
  currently supported in natural language search, the Iris AI Assistant, or Agent experiences"
  ([help](https://support.docusign.com/s/document-item?language=en_US&bundleId=map6bcbece5-da6c-428b-b6c2-a21350aa847f&topicId=con5595e6f4-1361-4918-bb6d-feb76db37266.html&_LANG=enus)). An agent judges clauses from the document's TEXT (system_dms_get_documents), as
  third-party-paper-triage does, never from the 13 standard clause columns.

## Spec fields

`assets/agents/specs/<id>.json`. The compiler refuses a key not listed here (a typo or an unsupported
feature is an error, never silently dropped), a missing required key, and a wrong JSON type.
"Proved" means a verify report under `assets/agents/verify/` passed with it.

| Key | Type | Required | Compiles to | Proved? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | nothing (the file name; the report's name) | — |
| `name` | string: letters, digits, spaces; ≤ 50 (lab prefix counted); not blank | yes | `meta.displayName`; the key `<snake name>_<ms>`; YAML `name` | yes, every report |
| `description` | string, ≤ 1000 | yes (may be empty) | `meta.description`, YAML `description` | yes |
| `instructions` | markdown: a string (verbatim), or an array of blocks; not blank | yes | YAML `instructions` as a literal block. An array item is one paragraph, heading or list item: items are joined by a blank line, except consecutive list items and table rows (`instructionsOf`) | yes. The editor reads markdown (lab, 2026-10-24) — see "Instructions are markdown" below |
| `capabilities` | array of capability ids (table below), no repeats; may be empty | yes | `meta.toolSet` (one id each) and YAML `tools` (every tool each grants) | all ten store, publish and open in the editor with no errors (lab specs, one capability each, 2026-10-24). Live answers only for Find Agreements, Party Insights, Review Documents and none; the acting, asking and CRM ones are never run |
| `extraTools` | array of `EXTRA_TOOLS` ids (11 read tools) | no | more YAML `tools` | `system_ask_sierra`, `system_iam_search_agreements_nl` (capabilities guide). The four added 2026-10-25 (reports, reporting agreements, directory users, entity store read) await lab spec `zz-extra-tools`. The other five are not proved |
| `acts` | boolean | when a capability writes (and only then) | nothing — a guard | — |
| `starterPrompts` | array of ≤ 3 non-blank strings, each ≤ 200 | no | `meta.starterPrompts` ("In chat") | stored: yes (up to 3); shown in the editor: checked by the editor gate from 2026-10-24 on |
| `outputs` | array of `{ name, format, description }`: name a variable name (letter, then letters/digits/_), unique; format `string` \| `boolean` \| `number`; description non-blank | no | `meta.maestroOutputs` ("In a workflow"); in a workflow, variables typed String / Boolean / Float | stored: all three formats; in a workflow: imported and on the canvas (never run) |
| `inWorkflow` | boolean | no (default true) | `meta.isMaestroEnabled` ("In a workflow"). `false` is a chat-only agent: no `outputs`, and a workflow's Execute AI Agent step naming it is refused | not yet (library spec renewal-terms-chat) |
| `icon` | string, an icon file name | no (default `Unity.svg`) | `meta.iconName` | only the default is proved. Names in use on legacy: Unity, Hub, Analyze, Trust, CustomerExperienceCX, Options, Balance_Alt, Conversation02, Top, Balance, Downsize, Legal (`.svg`). The value is not checked, and the full icon list is not in the app's bundle as file names |
| `summary` | string | no | nothing (the gallery tile) | — |
| `standing` | boolean | no | nothing (lives in the account, not a lab copy) | — |
| `testPrompt` | string | no | nothing (what the test gate asks) | — |
| `copiedFrom` | a ready-to-deploy agent's key (`system_…`) | no | `meta.copiedFromSystemAgent`, as a Duplicate of a Featured agent is saved (B4-A5) | — |
| `testExpect` | string or array of strings, non-empty; needs `testPrompt` | no | nothing — the test gate FAILS unless the answer contains each (case-insensitive). Without it the gate only checks that an answer exists, which passed "Not in my knowledge source" | — |
| `testAgreements` | array of agreement titles on the test account (exact, else the one title containing it); needs `testPrompt` | no | nothing — agent-verify indexes them (runtime `knowledge/ensure-indexed`, then `indexing-status` until complete) and sends them with the test prompt in the agui call's `forwarded_props.retrieval.sources` (`agreement_documents`), as Test ▸ + ▸ Add Agreements does (harvest 2026-11-09) | — |
| `testCases` | array of `{ prompt, expect?, agreements? }` (`expect` and `agreements` as `testExpect` and `testAgreements`) | no | nothing — agent-verify asks each after the `testPrompt`, in a fresh Test chat (the editor reopened); the test gate passes only when every case does. One case per answer the agent must tell apart (`dpa-coverage-check`: on file, referenced only, not needed) | — |
| `knowledge` | array of `{ file, name? }`: `file` under `assets/agents/knowledge/`, a PDF, TXT, DOC, DOCX or CSV; `name` the file name shown (default the file's); the agent needs at least one capability | no | an uploaded document per file, a knowledge base listing them, YAML `knowledge_bases` and `meta.knowledgeSourceKey` — see "Knowledge sources" | PROVED end to end (lab spec `zz-knowledge-tools`, 2026-10-25): stored, shown in the editor, and quoted by the Test panel. Needs at least one capability — refused otherwise, since without tools the file is never searched |

Fixed by the compiler, not by the spec: `meta.author`, `meta.purpose: "demo"`, `meta.isMaestroEnabled:
true` (the editor's default for every new agent), `kind: Prompt`.

**Chat, workflow or both** (`starts` in `gallery/agent-configs/index.json`, 2026-11-06: not
every agent should have a chat prompt). `captures/agent-gallery-data.ts` derives it from the spec: no
`outputs` (or `inWorkflow: false`) → `chat`; outputs and no capabilities → `workflow` (it reads only
what a workflow step hands it, e.g. Address Splitter); outputs and capabilities → `both`. Agent Studio
has no such setting (every agent stays "Always available in Iris"); the class tells the companion
app's Try it what to show.

**Examples file** (`assets/agents/examples/<id>.json`, optional; copied into the index as `examples`).
It sits beside the spec, not in it, because a spec edit changes `specHash` and needs a live re-verify.
- `starts`: overrides the derived class, with `why` (Third Party Paper Triage → `workflow`: its
  instructions take a request id from the step).
- `chat`: `{ question, answer, documents, note? }` — a question about the Fontara portfolio, the answer
  to expect (checked against the documents' text), and the register file names it should read.
- `workflow`: `{ workflow, values, source, outputs }` — a library workflow that runs the agent, a Fontara
  value for each `{{variable}}` in that workflow's step prompt, where the values come from, and the
  outputs to expect (names must be the agent's outputs). The index gets the step's `prompt` and the
  filled `input`; the build fails on a workflow that does not run the agent or a missing value.

The compiler is stricter than the editor in one known place: an output's **Description** is optional
in the editor (only Name and Format carry an asterisk, gallery/automations/11c-agent-in-workflow-config.png).
The compiler requires one because it is what tells the agent what to put there.

## Writing instructions

Library agents follow the shape Agent Studio's own AI-assisted builder writes (measured 2026-10-25 with
`captures/recon-agent-generate.ts`, five prompts), plus a Rules section the builder lacks:

```text
You are the <Name> for Fontara. You <job> (one or two sentences).
<Invocation rule: when to use the tools, and when to answer directly.>

## Instructions are markdown

Measured on legacy with three lab agents (2026-10-24), each created from a spec and opened in the editor:

- **A single newline is not a line break.** Lines written one under another showed as one paragraph,
  numbered steps, bullets and table included. This is why the compiler joins array items with a
  blank line.
- **A blank line starts a paragraph**, but a blank line between numbered items makes each its own list,
  so every one shows "1.". Keep list items consecutive (the compiler does, for array items). Re-proved on Test 4
  (2026-11-13): the editor ignores an item's number (`2.` after a blank line also
  shows "1."), its Save draft writes such items `1. … 1. … 1.`, a tight list saves renumbered `1. 2. 3.` and `1)` saves
  as `1.`. validateAgent refuses a numbered list with blank lines between items; forContribution makes it tight
  (tightLists, #560 #562 #554).
- **`#` / `##` give Heading 1 / 2, `**bold**` and `*italic*` render, consecutive `- ` and `1.` lines are
  real lists.** `__underline__` stays literal, and a pipe table is literal text.

**What the toolbar stores** (2026-10-25, `captures/recon-agent-format.ts` on the standing host, which
was restored afterwards): Heading 2 is stored as `## `, bold as `**…**`, italic as `*…*`, bullet items as
`- ` and numbered items as `1. `/`2. `. The same markdown a spec writes. **Underline is stored as HTML,
`<u>…</u>`**, so a spec that wants underline writes `<u>…</u>`. The compiler passes it through
verbatim. **There are no tables**: a pasted table was stored as its cells' text run together.

**A hand Save draft rewrites the instructions to what the editor shows.** On a host written before
the blank-line join, every run of single-newline lines, a pipe table and a numbered list included, was
stored back as ONE line. Spec text written with blank lines (the compiler's join, above) is
what the editor shows, so it survives a hand save.

**The editor's revision, from its own code** (the `@agents/ui` 1.0.262 bundle, read 2026-10-25): it builds
`meta` from `author`, `displayName`, `description`, `purpose` (default `"demo"`) and `isMaestroEnabled`
(default true). It adds `copiedFromSystemAgent`, `iconName` and `maestroOutputs` only when set, keeps
starter prompts trimmed and non-empty, and carries `knowledgeSourceKey`, `toolSet` and
`mcpToolsetKeys`. The last is an MCP toolset field that no spec or account here uses yet. There is
no separate settings panel: the header's icon buttons are Agent Actions (Share) and Monitor Agent Activity.

## What the product offers that a spec cannot express

| Feature | Where | Why not |
|---|---|---|
| **Knowledge sources from cloud storage** — SharePoint, OneDrive, Dropbox, Google Drive, FileIO, Box (the "Select File" menu; all but SharePoint offered as "Install") | Editor ▸ Knowledge Sources ▸ + Add ▸ Select File | Each needs a connector installed and signed in to; local files are supported (see "Knowledge sources") |
| **Tables** in instructions | — | The editor has none. A pipe table shows as literal text, a pasted table is flattened, and a hand save joins a pipe table's rows into one line. Write a list instead |
| **Sharing** — a user or group with Can Use / Can Edit / Can Manage | Agent Actions ▸ Share (gallery/automations/11g2-agent-share-access-levels.png) | People and groups belong to one account; set them by hand after creating the agent |
| **Unpublish, Duplicate** | Card menu | Not built. A changed spec need not become a second agent: `agent-create.ts <spec> --key=<key>` writes it as a new revision of that agent (same name, or the reuse host, restored after) |
| **Customizing a pre-set agent** | Agents ▸ Featured | A Featured card opens the system agent read only (Save draft and Publish disabled); its menu's Duplicate opens an unsaved copy and Save draft creates a NEW agent (quota) whose meta has `copiedFromSystemAgent` and whose tools are every tool of its capabilities (B4-A2, B4-A5 on the lab account, 2026-11-02). A spec writes that meta with `copiedFrom` (proof on the second standing host, LAB-RULES). A system agent in a workflow step: `agent: "system_…"` (the picker lists the 4 system agents; they declare no outputs) |
| **Five catalog tools that write or pause** (`system_update_agreement`, `system_entity_store_save`, `system_approve_worksheet_create_params`, `system_hitl_ask_multi_question`, `system_hitl_log_support_ticket`) | API only — the editor offers capabilities | `extraTools` takes read tools only. All 65 catalog tools are now classified: 51 in capabilities, 11 pinned extras, these 5 refused. A tool's draft cannot be read ("Tools are system-only and do not support read-by-key operations"), so the classification is from the catalog's descriptions |
| **"Act as publisher / starter"** on an Execute AI Agent step (Manual and API starts) | Workflow Builder | The help documents it: "authorize the selected agent to act on behalf of a workflow system role in the Agent permissions step. Select either the workflow publisher or the user who starts the workflow" ([help](https://support.docusign.com/s/document-item?language=en_US&bundleId=map781cab17-20ee-4e52-a109-43201480b341&topicId=task-1036.html&_LANG=enus)). The lab saw no such choice, but on a Link start, which the help excludes. Not harvested; the compiler writes neither. Re-probe on a Manual and an API start |

The Sierra help agent once gave runtime limits for agents in workflows (10 MB requests, 5 MB outputs,
60 executions a minute, a 5-minute timeout, 3 retries). **No help page states them** (all 1,136
saved help and developer pages searched, 2026-10-28), so they are not used anywhere. What the help
does say: "Practical limits may apply to how many agents can be created or run"; Agent Studio is
available in North America (U.S. and Canada) with English-language agreements, on IAM Professional,
Enterprise, for Sales and Platform ([help](https://support.docusign.com/s/document-item?language=en_US&bundleId=map781cab17-20ee-4e52-a109-43201480b341&topicId=task-8.html&_LANG=enus)). Besides Draft and Published,
an agent can have the status **Testing** ([help](https://support.docusign.com/s/document-item?language=en_US&bundleId=map781cab17-20ee-4e52-a109-43201480b341&topicId=conbc9170cf-1abd-4047-a359-38a766d7ccaf.html&_LANG=enus)).

## What instructions did not fix

Verified live 2026-11-05 on Test 1, each re-run three or more times after each instruction change; the same list is in the vault note *Docusign products* ▸ AI agents. Rows: `agent.limit.tracked-obligations`, `agent.limit.date-arithmetic`, `agent.limit.counts`, `agent.limit.answer-corrections`.

- **Agents can't read tracked obligations.** The agreement tools return none, though Track obligations was on and the agreements showed them on their Obligations tab. An agent told to prefer them computed the dates from the clauses. Where a date must be right, the demo quotes the Obligations tab; the agent's dates are a cross-check.
- **Date arithmetic slips.** After four rounds of step-by-step date instructions with a worked example, the Account Brief's dates (a period across a month end, N days after a date) still differed by days from the Obligations tab in most runs: 5 Dec and 5 Jan, or 30 Dec and 30 Jan, where the tab said 3 Dec and 2 Jan. The Breach Notice Clock labelled a 72-hour deadline from 21:00 on Wednesday 4 November as Sunday (it is Saturday). Told to work out each date, then its weekday by stepping from the starting weekday, it was right in most later runs, but one run copied the weekday from the instruction's own worked example and shifted every date after it. Keep worked examples off real dates. One instruction held: days left against a stated date were right once the agent had to write the days left beside each date.
- **Counts slip.** The Breach Notice Clock wrote "12 customers" for 12 agreements across 8 customers. Told to count customers, it still headed 8 customer lines with 7, 8, 9 or 10 across seven runs. Name what to count, and check the count against the lines.
- **Window edges get corrected in the answer.** An agent sorting certificates into "ending within 30 days" wrote "None", then "Wait correction: 9 November 2026 is within 30 days", in the answer itself. Tell it to fill each bucket before writing, with no thinking aloud, and check the answer for it.
